stem.text: Selected values of a function f are given in the table. The function f is not defined at \( x = 0 \). What does the table suggest about \( \lim_{x \to 0} f(x) \)?

answer_key.label: The table suggests that the limit does not exist, because the outputs approach different values on the two sides of x = 0.

worked_solution.text: From the left, the outputs -2.9500, -2.0905, -2.0090, -2.0009 approach -2.
worked_solution.rule_named: reading a table from one side

worked_solution.text: From the right, the outputs -3.2500, -3.0205, -3.0020, -3.0002 approach -3.
worked_solution.rule_named: reading a table from one side

worked_solution.text: The two sides approach different values, so the table suggests the two sided limit does not exist.
worked_solution.rule_named: two sided limit exists only when the one sided limits agree

options.label: The table suggests that the limit is -2, because the outputs approach -2 from the left of x = 0.
options.derivation: the value the left hand rows approach reported as the two sided limit

options.label: The table suggests that the limit is -3, because the outputs approach -3 from the right of x = 0.
options.derivation: the value the right hand rows approach reported as the two sided limit
